name: Cryptographic Protocols
description: Design and analysis of cryptographic protocols such as TLS, key exchange, messaging, and PKI.
narrative:
The earliest papers in this list, from 2018, already reveal that "cryptographic protocols" at the top venues had split into two big currents. One current is the explosion of blockchain and distributed-ledger work: OmniLedger (S&P 2018) and RapidChain (CCS 2018) both attacked the scalability problem by sharding a permissionless ledger so it could approach Visa-like throughput, while Arbitrum (USENIX 2018) tackled smart contracts that are both scalable and private. The other current is classic protocol design and analysis: practical threshold ECDSA with trustless setup (CCS 2018) and two-party threshold ECDSA from standard assumptions (S&P 2018) made distributed signing deployable, and secure-computation work like Compressing Vector OLE (CCS 2018) and HyCC (CCS 2018) pushed MPC toward practicality. At the same time, attack-and-analysis papers grounded the field in reality: The Dangers of Key Reuse exposed practical attacks on IPsec IKE (USENIX 2018), and formal modeling appeared via the distance-bounding analysis (USENIX 2018).

By 2019-2020 the field matured along both lines. On consensus and BFT, Flexible BFT (CCS 2019) and Sync HotStuff (S&P 2020) simplified and strengthened Byzantine fault tolerance, setting up the throughput-focused designs that followed. Formal verification became a marquee result, with the component-based analysis of 5G-AKA (NDSS 2019) finding flaws in a standard headed for billions of devices, echoed on the implementation side by protocol state fuzzing of DTLS (USENIX 2020). Real-world breakage stayed prominent through Dragonblood against WPA3's Dragonfly handshake (S&P 2020) and BIAS impersonation attacks on Bluetooth (S&P 2020). Meanwhile threshold cryptography and distributed key generation moved from theory to systems: Asynchronous DKG (CCS 2020) and Towards Scalable Threshold Cryptosystems (S&P 2020) made the trusted-dealer assumption avoidable at scale, and DECO (CCS 2020) cleverly turned TLS sessions into provable oracles of web data.

From 2021 onward the center of gravity shifted toward making these building blocks fast, composable, and economically robust. Payment-channel and cross-chain protocols matured with A2L's anonymous atomic locks (S&P 2021) and Universal Atomic Swaps (S&P 2022), while MAD-HTLC (S&P 2021) reframed security in game-theoretic, incentive terms by showing HTLCs are cheap to attack. Consensus reached a new plateau with DAG-based Bullshark (CCS 2022) and throughput-oblivious Dumbo-NG (CCS 2022), and Ebb-and-Flow Protocols (S&P 2021) resolved the availability-versus-finality dilemma. Distributed randomness and key generation became headline systems results through Spurt (S&P 2022) and Practical Asynchronous DKG (S&P 2022). The same period saw cryptographic protocols meet machine learning, as Eluding Secure Aggregation (CCS 2022) showed how a malicious server can break federated-learning privacy. The arc, then, runs from sharded ledgers and deployable signing schemes, through rigorous formal analysis and high-profile real-world breaks, to today's emphasis on scalable asynchronous consensus, incentive-aware channel protocols, and threshold infrastructure that underpins the whole stack.

milestones.title: OmniLedger: A Secure, Scale-Out, Decentralized Ledger via Sharding
milestones.note: set the template for scaling permissionless ledgers via sharding toward Visa-like throughput

milestones.title: The Dangers of Key Reuse: Practical Attacks on IPsec IKE
milestones.note: showed real-world deployed key-exchange (IPsec IKE) was breakable, keeping attack analysis central to the field

milestones.title: Component-Based Formal Analysis of 5G-AKA: Channel Assumptions and Session Confusion
milestones.note: brought rigorous formal analysis to a flagship standard (5G-AKA) before billions would deploy it

milestones.title: Dragonblood: Analyzing the Dragonfly Handshake of WPA3 and EAP-pwd
milestones.note: broke the new WPA3 Dragonfly handshake, a landmark real-world protocol failure

milestones.title: Asynchronous Distributed Key Generation for Computationally-Secure Randomness, Consensus, and Threshold Signatures
milestones.note: first asynchronous DKG, removing the trusted-dealer bottleneck for threshold systems

milestones.title: DECO: Liberating Web Data Using Decentralized Oracles for TLS
milestones.note: turned ubiquitous TLS sessions into provable oracles, bridging classic protocols with decentralized applications

milestones.title: MAD-HTLC: Because HTLC is Crazy-Cheap to Attack
milestones.note: reframed payment-channel security in game-theoretic, incentive terms rather than purely cryptographic ones

milestones.title: Bullshark: DAG BFT Protocols Made Practical
milestones.note: made DAG-based asynchronous BFT practical, marking the modern high-throughput consensus plateau
